tweet_summary: An Iran-war account claims 'Iran has destroyed Israeli air defense systems' and that Hezbollah is now 'raining missiles on Central Israel where 40% of the population lives,' over an Al Jazeera broadcast clip about rockets hitting central Israel.
why_note_decision: A note is warranted because the headline factual claim is inverted: it was ISRAEL/the U.S. that devastated IRAN's air defenses in the Feb-Mar 2026 campaign (officials/analysts cited ~80-92% degradation of Iran's missile/drone launch capacity and air defenses), not the reverse. There is no credible reporting that Iran destroyed Israel's air-defense systems. The secondary claim is more defensible: Hezbollah did strike Israel in early March 2026, and the embedded Al Jazeera report itself says the targeted central region holds ~44% of Israelis — so the '40%/central Israel' element is roughly accurate and not the thing to correct. The original note correctly inverted the air-defense claim but relied on live-blog URLs that raters flagged as missing/unreliable.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note corrects the inverted core claim — i.e. it states that Israel/the U.S. degraded IRAN's air defenses (not the other way around), ideally with a figure (~80% or higher) from a credible, stable source (Wikipedia '2026 Iran war', Reuters/AP/Britannica, or an official statement), NOT a bare live-blog link. The note must AVOID the original's sourcing weakness (two liveblog entries). It should NOT over-correct the Hezbollah/central-Israel element: Hezbollah did fire on Israel and central Israel ~ 44% of the population, so flatly denying any Hezbollah strikes would be wrong. FAIL if it affirms 'Iran destroyed Israeli air defenses,' cites only unstable liveblogs, or wrongly denies the Hezbollah strikes.
reference_note: This is reversed: in the Feb-Mar 2026 war, Israeli and U.S. strikes degraded IRAN's air defenses and sharply cut its missile/drone launch capacity (officials and analysts cited ~80-90% reductions); there is no credible report that Iran destroyed Israel's air-defense systems. Hezbollah did launch missiles toward central Israel, which holds roughly 44% of the population. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war https://www.npr.org/2026/03/02/g-s1-112140/hezbollah-strikes-israel

original_unhelpful_note.text: The post inaccurately claims Iran destroyed Israeli air defenses. Actually, Israel destroyed ~80% of Iran's air defenses. Hezbollah has launched missiles at central Israel (home to ~40-44% of Israelis).    https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-chief-says-israel-has-destroyed-80-of-irans-air-defense-systems  https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/2026-03-09/live-updates-889301
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Rated notHelpfulSourcesMissingOrUnreliable (19) as the dominant tag. The substance is correct (it inverts the false air-defense claim and accepts the true Hezbollah element), but it cites two live-blog entries — transient, hard-to-verify URLs that raters deemed unreliable/missing. The fix is a stable, authoritative citation for the ~80% figure rather than liveblogs.

fact_check.claim_verdict: false core claim (inverted); secondary Hezbollah claim true
fact_check.notes: Feb 28, 2026: ~900 US/Israeli strikes hit Iran's missiles, air defenses, infrastructure; analysts/officials cite ~80-92% drops in Iran's missile/drone launch capacity. No reporting that Iran destroyed Israel's air defenses. Hezbollah did strike Israel (Mar 2, NPR); the embedded Al Jazeera report puts central Israel at ~44% of population. So only the air-defense claim is false; the Hezbollah/central-Israel part is roughly right.

importance.lens_rationale: Wartime battlefield-status misinformation shapes public understanding and escalation pressure; correcting an inverted claim about who holds the military advantage is genuinely valuable.
